title: Dry mouth and mouth care when eating or drinking stops

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe recognized patterns but do not supply firsthand room texture.
The record must not be used to diagnose, time, or manage a particular death.
Treatment, legal, ritual, and emergency decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: A person near death stops eating or drinking, has a dry mouth or lips, and carers shift from meals and glasses of water toward mouth comfort, moistening, lip care, and care-team guidance.
ordinary_language_queries: should I give water if they cannot swallow

content_layers.observation_text: Public sources distinguish the expected loss of appetite and drinking from the comfort problem of a dry mouth; they commonly point toward mouth moistening and care-team guidance rather than forcing food or fluids.
content_layers.source_synthesis: NHS, NHS inform, Hospice UK, Palliative Care Australia, and Marie Curie converge that eating/drinking often lessens near death, swallowing can become difficult, and mouth comfort remains important.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: This record prevents the corpus from treating “stopped eating” as only a symptom. It is also a family moral crisis: feeding once meant love, and then comfort may require not feeding.

what_this_is_not: not permission to force food or fluid
not a hydration or medication plan
not proof the person is suffering from thirst in the way witnesses fear
not a universal rule for every illness or culture
uncertainties: Artificial hydration questions are ethically and clinically context-specific.
The exact boundary between safe sips and unsafe swallowing requires local care-team assessment.
Future witness records should preserve how guilt and love attach to feeding.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should validate why not eating or drinking feels frightening, then separate food-as-love from mouth-comfort-as-care.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect demonstration scripts, family guilt language, and oral-care practices without becoming a procedural manual.
language_notes: Use “mouth comfort” as a bridge term.
Do not use “starving” except as a reader query routed to clarification.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the v2 witnessed-moment schema. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical safety review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent or worried readers to qualified local support.
